chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: British tour: sidemen, Jack Jackson and the Scottish response
summary: She took Earl Hyde and George Duvivier, toured with Jack Jackson and found fans in Scotland who knew all her songs.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What musicians did you take with you?

I had -- when I first went I took Earl Hyde on drums, and George Duvivier, who's today one of the greatest and one of the finest bass players around, amongst the finest. They went with me the first time, and the second time, for that matter. And it was just tremendous, really. The response was so very great, until I couldn't believe it, when you'd play these halls over there, you know. I guess this was their chief form of entertainment. I'm trying to remember what they call them. They don't call them vaudeville houses. They call them something else. But anyway, these people would respond, and they knew, they knew you, who you were. They knew who I was and they knew my records, my works, and right today I still hear from these people.

Incidentally, there was one man that was a marvelous -- he was just a marvelous performer, musician, impresario, band leader, orchestra leader, disc jockey, whatever. His name was Jack Jackson, and Jack Jackson was very, very popular in

England at the time. So Jack Jackson travelled with me. He toured the whole scene with me, he and his wife, each time. And we had the most marvelous time and the most wonderful -- Jack Jackson just passed, I think, this past year. But he was a wonderful, wonderful guy, and I did get to meet many of the English musicians, people that were very important in the circuit, you know, and I had a chance to really see just what and how much they appreciate our American music. They really -- I mean there's no question about it. They are deeply concerned and they are really -- they are really responsive to what you do.

Scotland was -- I certainly didn't expect this in Scotland. When I got there and they knew every -- they knew my work. They just absolutely -- Nellie this and Nellie, Nellie, Nellie, play this, and they knew the songs that I did, could sing them right along, and this one little fellow, right now, he was just a youngster at that time, he was from Liverpool. Liverpool was my very first engagement in England, was Liverpool, and he and his little friend followed us all over, you know, all over England, everywhere we would go. Every Sunday they would come to see us in a different place.
